findings.description: Helper _compute_tolerances (lines 481-485) calls torch.cuda.get_device_capability(0) to loosen tolerances on CUDA SM86. The catalog lists get_device_capability under category_a.same_name (replaceable) but ALSO under category_c.cuda.device_properties, and the return type differs per backend (tuple[int,int] on CUDA/MTIA vs dict[str,Any] on accelerator/XPU), so a naive torch.accelerator.get_device_capability replacement would break the `== (8, 6)` comparison.
findings.recommendation: Make _compute_tolerances accelerator-agnostic: guard the SM86 branch with a device_type=='cuda' check before comparing the capability tuple (device-type-aware comparison). The 5 calling tests (test_cnn_model_sum, test_cnn_model_mean, test_instance_norm_model, test_group_norm_model, test_layer_norm_model) stay Strategy2 - the tolerance tweak is a precision nicety, not the subject of the tests.

findings.description: test_expanded_weight_forward contains an in-body device conditional `if "cuda" in device and "max_norm" in sample_input.kwargs and "padding_idx" in sample_input.kwargs: self.skipTest(...)` for non-deterministic CUDA embedding (issue #74679). Per the classification guide, a device conditional in the test body does NOT make a test Strategy3.
findings.recommendation: Keep as-is (Strategy2). The embedding skip is also mirrored by a DecorateInfo in common_methods_invocations.py (line 21822), so leave the in-body skip untouched.

findings.description: Legacy module-level nn-tests harness (lines 1022-1055) dynamically attaches CPU and CUDA-named tests (<name>, <name>_multiple_inputs, <name>_cuda_double) to TestExpandedWeightModule via setattr, hardcoding the device strings 'cpu'/'cuda' and gating the CUDA variants on TEST_CUDA. The comment at line 1017 says these should become ModuleInfo tests. This is the ONLY consumer of the TEST_CUDA import and the source of hardcoded 'cuda' test names.
findings.recommendation: Out of scope for the S1/S2/S3 strategy conversion (the dynamic tests are not static `def test_` methods), but flag for follow-up: modernizing this harness to ModuleInfo-based tests would remove the hardcoded device strings, the CUDA-named variants, and the TEST_CUDA dependency. Keep the loop and the TEST_CUDA import for now.

findings.description: class TestContext: pass (lines 44-45) is an empty placeholder with no tests. It is never instantiated, never referenced, and is not part of instantiate_device_type_tests. Assessment phase counted it as a class (test_count 0).
findings.recommendation: Remove the dead TestContext class as part of the refactoring.

findings.description: TEST_CUDA is imported from common_cuda and used at exactly one site: line 1049 in the legacy module-level test generation loop (`if TEST_CUDA and test.test_cuda:`). No test is being converted from S1 to S2 in this file (all tests are already device-parametrized in instantiate_device_type_tests classes), so TEST_CUDA does NOT become stale as a result of the strategy conversion.
findings.recommendation: Keep the TEST_CUDA import while the legacy loop is retained (do NOT remove it in this refactor). It becomes removable only if the legacy harness is modernized (see finding at line 1022).

findings.description: tf32_off() decorator from common_cuda is applied to 6 Strategy2 tests (test_cnn_model_sum, test_cnn_model_mean, test_instance_norm_model, test_group_norm_model, test_layer_norm_model, test_module) as a CUDA TF32 precision control. It is a test decorator, not a Category C API call in the test bodies, so it does NOT make these tests Strategy3 and does not require keeping @onlyCUDA (none exists).
findings.recommendation: Retain the tf32_off import and all 6 @tf32_off() decorators unchanged. Do not flag these tests as Category C.

findings.description: @onlyCUDA / @onlyOn audit: no @onlyCUDA or @onlyOn decorators exist anywhere in this file, so there is nothing to enlarge to @onlyAccelerator. All device-scoped tests are already plain `device`-parametrized methods in instantiate_device_type_tests classes.
findings.recommendation: None - no whitelist decorators to change.

findings.description: Blacklist-skip audit: no @skipXPU, @skipCUDAIf, @skipMPS, @skipMeta, or @onlyNativeDeviceTypesAnd decorators exist in this file. The only skip decorator is @skipIfTorchDynamo (line 330, a dynamo skip, unrelated to device).
findings.recommendation: None - no blacklist skips to preserve.

findings.description: External reference: TestExpandedWeightFunctional is referenced by a DecorateInfo entry in torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py (line 21822) that skips test_expanded_weight_forward for the nn.functional.embedding OpInfo. DecorateInfo matches against the generic class name, so any rename of TestExpandedWeightFunctional would break this skip unless the DecorateInfo is updated.
findings.recommendation: Keep the original class names for all classes (no renaming). Renaming is optional per the workflow, and here it would create external-reference churn in common_methods_invocations.py with no benefit since the file is already uniformly Strategy2.

summary: The file is already almost entirely Strategy2 (accelerator-agnostic). All 27 top-level test methods live in classes that are instantiated via instantiate_device_type_tests with `device` (and dtype/op/module_info) parameters already present; no test is decorated with @onlyCPU, @onlyCUDA, @onlyOn, or any blacklist skip, and no S1->S2 or whitelist-enlargement conversion is needed. The only per-test device work is mechanical: test_per_sample_api_failing, test_per_sample_api_compute_batch_size, test_per_sample_api_compute_batch_size_not_pytreeable and test_group_norm_error lack a `device` parameter (but are in instantiate_device_type_tests classes, so they are already S2) and only need `device` threaded into their tensor creation. The ContextManagerTests class is a legacy TestBase harness whose two methods (test_context_manager, test_context_manager_multiple_inputs) are device-aware templates consumed by the module-level setattr loop that attaches CPU and CUDA-named variants to TestExpandedWeightModule; it stays S2. No class splits are recommended and no class renames are recommended (TestExpandedWeightFunctional has an external DecorateInfo reference). The only stale symbol is the empty dead class TestContext. TEST_CUDA and tf32_off imports remain live (used by the legacy loop and precision decorators respectively); TEST_MPS/TEST_XPU/onlyOn/device_type are not present. Two device-specific points flagged for the coder: _compute_tolerances uses torch.cuda.get_device_capability (return-type hazard if swapped for torch.accelerator), and test_expanded_weight_forward has an in-body CUDA skipTest that must stay.
